skills.source: R6 split (reports/scope/04-branch-map.md): Detect an inconsistent measurement innovation

edges.rationale: The innovation and its covariance are produced by the state estimator's update step.
Fusing nonlinear measurements includes testing inconsistent measurements; this is that test, split out and taught first on the linear case.
A gate threshold is a hypothesis test; its false-alarm rate is a type I error.

specification.name: Detect an inconsistent measurement innovation
specification.demonstration: For a stated linear Gaussian filter, compute each measurement's innovation and innovation covariance, form the normalized innovation squared, and compare it with a chi-square gate fixed in advance from the measurement dimension and a stated false-alarm rate; classify a synthetic sequence that includes injected outliers, and explain why a rejected measurement alone does not distinguish a sensor fault from a wrong noise or motion model.
specification.origin: scope R6 split of P09, completions edition 07

skills.source: R12 new skill (reports/scope/04-branch-map.md): Distinguish coupling misalignment from backlash

edges.rationale: Separating lost motion from elastic deflection comes first; misalignment is the third effect to tell apart.
Misalignment shows up as radial load on the shaft supports chosen there.
Telling misalignment from backlash is one diagnosis an integrated failure may need, but not every joint has a separate shaft coupling.

specification.name: Distinguish coupling misalignment from backlash
specification.demonstration: Given a motor, coupling and output shaft with stated measurements of output angle against input angle over full revolutions and at direction reversals, plus shaft-support load or vibration readings, attribute the error to backlash (a dead band at reversal, independent of shaft angle), misalignment (an error and radial load that repeat once or twice per revolution, with no dead band) or both; name the measurement that would separate them when the data cannot.

assessment_contract.task: Given a motor, coupling and output shaft with stated measurements of output angle against input angle over full revolutions and at direction reversals, plus shaft-support load or vibration readings, attribute the error to backlash (a dead band at reversal, independent of shaft angle), misalignment (an error and radial load that repeat once or twice per revolution, with no dead band) or both; name the measurement that would separate them when the data cannot.
